subject: Uptime banding + rapid-response retainer: packaging questions
messages:
From: Emma Stone <emma@cloudnative.io>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Cc: CloudNative Procurement <procurement@cloudnative.io>
Date: 2026-10-29T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: Clarification on uptime bands + retainer structure

Hi Monica,

Thanks for the SLA draft — we reviewed it with the platform team. A couple of points we need clarified before we loop in procurement:

- Can you explain how the uptime bands translate into blended credits? The table in v3 shows 99.95% / 99.9% / 99.5% but the credit math is not obvious to our finance folks.
- We're interested in a hybrid model: committed baseline + burst pool. Is there an example pricing row for a 2:1 burst-to-commit ratio?
- For the rapid-response retainer, can you confirm whether your on-call engineers rotate across timezones? We need guaranteed 24/7 coverage with overlap for PST/EET handoffs.

Attached the SLA draft with inline comments (sla-draft-v3.pdf). Procurement is copied on high-level commercial questions.

Appreciate a quick runbook or a short call this week.

Emma
Emma Stone
Head of Platform
CloudNative Inc.
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emma Stone <emma@cloudnative.io>, CloudNative Procurement <procurement@cloudnative.io>
Date: 2026-10-29T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Clarification on uptime bands + retainer structure

Team — looping you in for pricing + ops detail. Quick answers up front, then I'll send a short matrix back to Emma: 

1) Blended credits: we apply a sliding credit that scales by incident severity and band breach duration. Example (simplified): if committed band is 99.95% and observed monthly availability is 99.80%, the delta maps to the 99.9->99.5 slab and we apply the prorated credit percentage for that slab times committed spend. I'll attach a worked example.

2) Committed + burst: we can model a 2:1 burst-to-commit economically by charging committed at discounted unit rates and burst at on-demand rates with a cap. Suggest showing three rows: baseline-only, baseline+2:1 burst, and baseline+4:1 burst.

3) On-call coverage: Redwood operates regional on-call rotations. For customers requiring guaranteed 24/7 with timezone overlap (PST/EET), we propose a primary regional roster plus an overlap window (typically 4 hours) staffed by a cross-region on-call to handle handoffs. This is a premium add-on to the retainer.

Action items: Priyom — can you produce the numeric examples (credit math + 2:1 burst pricing) and a short summary of global on-call ops? Karthik — legality/contract note: does the credit calculation need tighter language around measurement windows? Vanessa — I'll want a short customer-facing one-pager for Emma.

Monica

On Thu, Oct 29, 2026 at 08:14 AM Emma Stone <emma@cloudnative.io> wrote:
> (quoted above)
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-30T09:36:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Clarification on uptime bands + retainer structure (worked numbers)

Monica — attached two worksheets: retainer-pricing-grid.xlsx (tabbed with sample rows) and a short worked example pasted below.

Worked example (monthly):
- Committed spend: $150k (baseline)
- Expected availability target: 99.95%
- Observed availability: 99.80% -> shortfall maps to credit slab => 5% credit on committed spend (example slab rule)
- Credit = $150k * 0.05 = $7.5k applied as invoice offset the following month.

Baseline + 2:1 burst row (sample):
- Baseline commit: $150k/month @ $2.00 per unit
- Burst pool (2x capacity): priced at $3.50 per unit up to a 2x cap; after cap, on-demand pricing applies. Effective blended unit cost in scenario where 30% of tokens hit burst = $2.35/unit.

On-call ops summary (short):
- Two regional rosters (NA / EMEA) + a small cross-regional overlap team.
- Overlap window suggested: 04:00–08:00 UTC (covers late PST -> early EET handoff).
- Escalation coverage: L1 triage in-region, L2 engineering cross-region, L3 on-call lead with 30-minute response SLA for sev-1s (as part of retainer).

I'll push the XLSX and a single-page example to Monica for customer share.

Priyom
From: Emma Stone <emma@cloudnative.io>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Cc: CloudNative Procurement <procurement@cloudnative.io>, Jordan Miles <j.miles@lawsonllc.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T07:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Clarification on uptime bands + retainer structure

Thanks Priyom — this is helpful. Procurement wants a concise definition of the measurement window (UTC vs rolling 30-day), and explicit examples of how credits show on invoices (line item vs netting). Also: our legal has a standard requirement to cap aggregate credits at 30% of monthly committed spend; would Redwood be comfortable reflecting a cap in contract language?

Jordan (copied) is our procurement counsel — can he coordinate redlines?

Can we get a short 15-minute call Thurs 11/4 to finalize? Prefer 9am PT.

Emma

--
Emma Stone
Head of Platform, CloudNative Inc.
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Stone <emma@cloudnative.io>, CloudNative Procurement <procurement@cloudnative.io>, Jordan Miles <j.miles@lawsonllc.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-02T16:22:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Clarification on uptime bands + retainer structure — cap and invoice mechanics

Emma / Jordan / Procurement — thanks for the quick turn. Confirming next steps and our positions so procurement has something to redline: 

- Measurement window: Redwood proposes a rolling 30-day measurement window by default (UTC timestamps). We can add an option for calendar-month measurement for customers that require it; that will be flagged in the SOW.
- Invoice mechanics: credits are shown as a separate invoice line item ("Service Credits - SLA") for transparency; we can also offer netting if preferred, but procurement must select netting in the billing addendum.
- Credit cap: we are willing to accept a 30% monthly committed-spend cap for this account provided the retainer tier is increased to the Premium Rapid-Response level (adds the overlap team and advanced telemetry). If CloudNative prefers the lower retainer tier, cap would be 20%.

I've attached an updated SLA excerpt and pricing grid (sla-draft-v3.pdf redlined + retainer-pricing-grid.xlsx). Can Jordan send an initial redline by end of day Friday so we can lock the 11/4 9am PT slot?

Proposed call: Thu Nov 4, 2026 — 09:00 PT / 12:00 ET / 17:00 CET (15 minutes).

Thanks — Monica
